subject: Operator handback, crypto safeguards & order form redlines
messages:
From: Susan Patel <susan.patel@medtechhealth.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medtechhealth.com
Date: Thu, 13 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on operator handback + crypto controls for private hosting addendum

Hi David / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at MedTech Health is optimistic about a private VPC deployment for our inference workloads. Procurement asked me to consolidate a few technical/legal questions so we can progress the Order Form + MSA addenda review. High-level asks below:

1) Operator handback: We need clarity on the proposed operator-snapshot process and whether Redwood will (a) deliver an encrypted snapshot to our S3 with customer-managed KMS, or (b) provide a sealed snapshot to a neutral escrow agent. Our security/compliance team is leaning toward customer-imported, customer-KMS encryption for forensic evidence.

2) Crypto safeguards: Is there a documented flow for key custody transfers during onboarding and decommissioning? Specifically, we want to confirm that operator keys are never stored in plaintext in the Redwood control plane and that any HSM interactions are auditable.

3) Order Form redlines: Procurement has three redline requests around termination handback timelines, temporary audit access windows, and a carve-out for emergency access for safety-related incidents. We attached a spreadsheet with marked-up timelines.

Can you confirm who we should expect from legal/ops to review these items and whether Redwood can provide a short technical appendix (1–2 pages) that maps the snapshot/handback options to the MSA exhibits? We’d like to get a draft back to our legal team before the Friday procurement sync.

Attachments: OrderForm_20251113_markups.xlsx

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call if that helps.

Best,
Susan Patel
Director, Procurement
MedTech Health
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Susan Patel <susan.patel@medtechhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Nov 2025 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on operator handback + crypto controls for private hosting addendum

Susan — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (legal) and Connor (ops) to respond to the specifics. Quick answers while they weigh in: 

- Operator snapshot: we support delivering an encrypted snapshot to customer-owned S3 using customer-managed KMS (preferred by many customers). We can also facilitate an escrow deposit with a third party; that’s treated as an alternative in the addendum.

- Key custody: Redwood uses HSM-backed key wrapping for any platform-managed secrets and we can provide audit logs for HSM calls. We do not persist customer KMS master keys. I’ll ask Connor to put together the short appendix mapping options to Exhibit A/B.

Marissa — can you confirm MSA language tolerance for (i) a customer-KMS delivery obligation, (ii) a neutral-escrow option that includes witness-signed receipts, and (iii) a time-limited emergency access carve-out? We’d prefer to bake the options into the Order Form so the procurement team can pick the path that fits their compliance posture.

I’ll also attach a draft redline set (Redwood_MSA_v2_redlines.pdf) once Marissa returns comments.

Best,
David Kim
Senior Director, Platform Partnerships
Redwood Inference

On Thu, 13 Nov 2025 at 09:12, Susan Patel <susan.patel@medtechhealth.com> wrote:

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Susan Patel <susan.patel@medtechhealth.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Nov 2025 14:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on operator handback + crypto controls for private hosting addendum

Susan — appreciate the summary. I reviewed Procurement’s spreadsheet and added legal positions inline; attaching: Redwood_MSA_v2_redlines.pdf and Operator_Runbook_Draft.docx. Key points (high level):

- Customer-KMS snapshot delivery: Acceptable. Proposed contract language: Redwood will encrypt snapshots using customer-provided KMS keys and deliver artifacts to the customer's designated storage endpoint within 5 business days of a valid handback trigger. (See section: Snapshot Delivery & Validation.)

- Neutral escrow: We can offer this as an optional Exhibit; the escrow path will require a mutually agreeable third-party custodian and a witnessed transfer protocol. For several of our customers the escrow route increases cost and complexity — we'll surface a cost estimate if MedTech wants to pursue.

- Emergency access carve-out: We can support a limited emergency access procedure tied to documented incident classification (safety/availability). We propose a two-step approval: (1) on-call engineering attestation + (2) senior legal sign-off from Redwood. Access will be strictly scoped, time-limited, and logged. We object to unconstrained access requests that circumvent the usual attestations.

- Audit access windows: We suggest a standard 48-hour temporary console access window for witness audits, with notice and a read-only role where possible. For on-prem deployments where a customer-run console is present, temporary credentials will be scoped to the audit task list.

Next steps I recommend:
- Connor to produce a 1–2 page technical appendix mapping (customer KMS vs escrow) and the HSM/audit logging artifacts.
- Legal to confirm agreed redlines and produce a clean MSA + Exhibit merge for Procurement.

Can we target EOD Friday for the appendix + clean redline packet so your procurement/legal can circulate? If you want to accelerate, I’m available for a 30-min touch on Friday morning.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Transactions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_v2_redlines.pdf; Operator_Runbook_Draft.docx

Date: Fri, 14 Nov 2025 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on operator handback + crypto controls for private hosting addendum

Marissa / David — this is helpful, thank you. Procurement likes the customer-KMS default path and will mark the neutral-escrow option as "optional" in our internal approval. A couple follow-ups from Procurement and Security: 

- Can the customer-KMS handback SLA be tightened to 3 business days for production-critical systems? They flagged 5 days as too long for regulated workloads.

- Procurement asked that any emergency access events trigger a joint post-incident review with MedTech Security and Redwood security within 72 hours.

We’ll aim to incorporate your redlines and the appendix into our internal packet and re-circulate by Monday for final sign-off. If you can share the appendix link and the updated redline PDF (DocuSign-ready) that would be great.

Thanks — I'll schedule that Friday morning call only if you post the appendix after hours.

Best,
Susan
Director, Procurement
MedTech Health
